correctness.rationale: For a consistent system the linear error projector is v_j v_j^T for a unit tangent v_j. Composing these rank-one matrices gives the endpoint outer product times the adjacent cosine factors, so a zero operator is equivalent to at least one adjacent orthogonal pair. At odd n the factor minimum is sin(pi/(2n)); its equality edges have modular steps ±(n−1)/2, forming one cycle by coprimality. Cutting and orienting it gives exactly 2n minimizing paths (including n=3). At n=2m the orthogonal pairs are disjoint. Compressing any j specified pairs gives 2^j(n−j)! orders, and binomial inversion of these joint counts yields every mass of X, including n=2. For j≤n^(1/3) the product over s<j of (1−s/(n−s)) expands as 1−j(j−1)/(2n)+O(j^4/n^2); the ratio product is at most 1, so factorial tails justify the summed error and dominated binomial inversion yields Poisson(1). The iid no-hit probability is (1−1/n)^(n−1) by constant conditional hazard; its first correction has the opposite sign from reshuffling's. The regular frame average of the projectors is I/2 for either parity, so iid exact squared-error contraction follows by conditioning. Independent bounded enumeration reproduced even n=4 counts [8,8,8], even n=8 counts [13824,15744,8064,2304,384], and 14 minimizing orders at n=7 (replay: /workspace/branches/87f708e6-b35f-423e-9ac7-3b1711c779b2/independent_check_record2.py and accompanying check_n*.txt). Read but did not execute the frozen verifier; its cosine tests are finite diagnostics, not independent matrix-product tests or an all-size proof. Termination here is of the whole error operator in exact arithmetic, not of a special starting vector or a perturbed system.
